lines.text: Freight broker C.H. Robinson owns very few trucks. In 2025 it still kept $1.7 billion from North American freight.
lines.say: Barely any trucks, yet this company kept one point seven billion.

lines.text: In 2025, shippers paid C.H. Robinson's North American unit $11.6 billion; after paying truckers, it kept $1.7 billion.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, shippers paid C H Robinson's North American unit eleven point six billion; after paying truckers, it kept one point seven.

lines.text: Shippers pay the broker, it pays truckers less and keeps the gap.
lines.say: Shippers pay the broker, it pays truckers less and keeps the gap.

lines.text: Hypothetical $1,000 load: the trucker gets $852; the broker keeps 14.8%, Robinson's 2025 North American average.
lines.say: On a hypothetical thousand-dollar load, the trucker gets eight hundred fifty-two dollars; the broker keeps fourteen point eight percent.

lines.text: That spread swings: 12.4% to 14.8% from 2021 to 2025 (C.H. Robinson NAST).
lines.say: That spread swings, from twelve point four to fourteen point eight percent.

lines.text: It bottomed in 2021, when costs outran prices.
lines.say: It bottomed in twenty twenty-one, when costs outran prices.

lines.text: Shipper contracts often run up to a year; Robinson buys most truck capacity at spot prices.
lines.say: Shipper contracts often run up to a year, but most trucks are bought spot.

lines.text: In Q2 2026, Robinson's truckload cost per mile jumped 29% while prices rose about 25%, and its North American margin fell to 13.1%.
lines.say: In the second quarter of twenty twenty-six, costs per mile jumped twenty-nine percent; its margin fell to thirteen point one percent.

lines.text: In August 2026, DAT had van spot rates at $2.19 a mile, 22 cents under the $2.41 contract average.
lines.say: In August twenty twenty-six, DAT had van spot at two nineteen a mile, twenty-two cents under contract.

post.title: A broker with few trucks kept $1.7B after paying truckers
post.ig:
C.H. Robinson owns very few trucks, yet after paying truckers its North American unit kept $1.71B of the $11.56B shippers paid it in 2025 (before its own staff and tech costs).

The model: shippers pay the broker, the broker hires a trucking company for less, and keeps the spread. In 2025 that averaged 14.8% (hypothetical $1,000 load: $852 to the trucker, $148 kept).
The spread swings: 12.4% in 2021, 14.8% in 2025, and 13.1% in Q2 2026 after truckload costs per mile jumped 29%.
In August 2026, DAT's van spot rate was $2.19 a mile vs $2.41 on contract.

Sources: C.H. Robinson 10-K filings (FY2021-FY2025), Q2 2026 results; DAT (Sept 2026).

Freight broker C.H. Robinson owns very few trucks, yet its North American unit kept $1.71 billion of $11.56 billion in 2025 revenue, a 14.8% spread between what shippers pay and what truckers get. That spread was as low as 12.4% in 2021, and fell to 13.1% in Q2 2026 from 14.8% a year earlier as carrier costs jumped; in August 2026 DAT put van spot rates at $2.19 a mile versus $2.41 on contract. Sources: C.H. Robinson 10-K filings and Q2 2026 results, DAT.
